anti_overlap: Leave save-format, key-stability, and migration-sequencing questions (geonameid rebuild timing, save v4 block ownership, positional-id re-keying blast radius) to the persistence/schema-evolution reviewer.

Leave 'does the roadmap's silence on a melange finding constitute an undisposed drop' and cross-checking the Tier-1 rung 2/3 scope boundary to the traceability reviewer; only raise a melange finding here when it bears directly on signal dynamics (e.g. f-029's regime-phase lockstep as a discrete-jump input to the pressure signal).

Don't argue over slice ordering or which slice should ship first -- take the proposed order as given and evaluate only whether the numeric/dynamical behavior inside slice 1 is sound and whether its done-criteria are a real detector of that behavior.
decision_lens: Every tunable write-back is modeled as a control loop: what drives the input signal, whether that signal is itself downstream of the loop's own output (closed-loop) or wholly exogenous (open-loop), what the erosion and recovery rates do to the steady state under the sample's real numbers, and whether a proposed pass/fail criterion can be satisfied by degenerate one-directional behavior instead of the two-directional 'tracks the pillar' dynamic the ruling claims.
focus: Whether the institution-lifecycle write-back (ruling 2, the actual lifecycle_step erosion/recovery constants in pillar.rs) and the coalition-bond decay it rides alongside are dynamically stable on the sample's real inputs, and whether slice 1's three sampler-number done-criteria (ruling 7) detect that the mechanism works as intended or merely that it is wired at all.
name: fd-governor-runaway
persona: Apply the perspective of a systems-dynamics and feedback-control analyst who has debugged runaway and oscillating loops in game economies and social simulations -- legitimacy death-spirals, inflation spirals, threshold ping-pong -- and reasons about gain, floor/ceiling clamps, and steady-state behavior from the actual constants and the actual observed inputs, not from the mechanism's stated intent.
review_areas: Whether lifecycle_step's constants (EROSION_EFF_PER_MONTH=0.010, EROSION_LEG_PER_MONTH=0.015, RECOVERY_PER_MONTH=0.005, erosion threshold 0.6, recovery threshold 0.3, floor 0.2, ceiling 0.9) produce a stable trajectory or a runaway/oscillation when driven by the sample's own leadership_pressure=0.69 against a 0.6 gate, and whether leadership_pressure is closed-loop (fed back from legitimacy/stability) or open-loop (purely exogenous) -- the runaway argument depends entirely on which.

Whether 'institution effectiveness and legitimacy show at least 50 distinct values across the 1,768' (ruling 7) is trivially satisfied by pure one-way erosion-to-floor (any per-institution pressure variance produces >50 distinct decaying values within one or two monthly ticks) without ever exercising the recovery branch -- i.e., whether the criterion can pass with the 'tracks the pillar' half of ruling 2 dead code.

Whether the observed macro instability in the sample (oil 42 -> 389 across 191 of 191 countries, stability index with 160 distinct values across 221 countries) feeds into protest_prob/legitimacy/stability and therefore into leadership_pressure, such that turning on the write-back rides on top of a substrate that is itself moving roughly 9x in seven months -- amplifying rather than reflecting an already-unstable base signal.

Whether 'coalition bonds form and at least one prunes' (ruling 7) is satisfied by a single passive-decay tick (0.015 trust/month for any bond not interacted-with, per coalitions.rs) firing once across the whole 193-day run, independent of whether the bond population as a whole is healthy, collapsing, or never forming in the first place.

Whether the erosion/recovery asymmetry (legitimacy erodes at 0.015/month, recovers at only 0.005/month -- 3x slower) is a deliberate texture choice or an unexamined default that, combined with a volatile economic substrate, biases every institution toward the floor over a long run regardless of what actually happens to leadership.

severity_examples.condition: Applies if leadership_pressure's inputs are themselves partly downstream of the same institutions' legitimacy/effectiveness, making the write-back a closed loop rather than the open-loop 'sim tracks pillar' framing ruling 2 implies.
severity_examples.scenario: leadership_pressure is computed in pillar.rs from protest_prob, legitimacy, and stability. If legitimacy feeds pressure and pressure erodes legitimacy in the same monthly step, that closes a loop; turning on institution_lifecycle_enabled() on a 193-day sample that already shows leadership_pressure=0.69 (above the 0.6 erosion gate) and oil at roughly 9x its start could drive legitimacy toward the 0.2 floor across most of the 1,768 institutions well before any of slice 1's other gates (determinism goldens, smoke test 11/11) would catch a collapsed number as distinct from a merely wrong one.

severity_examples.condition: Occurs whenever the sample's leadership_pressure distribution rarely or never drops below 0.3 for institutions that were previously above 0.6, which the 193-day sample's own reported 0.69 sustained pressure makes plausible.
severity_examples.scenario: The '>=50 distinct values' done-criterion is satisfiable by pure one-way erosion: every institution above the 0.6 pressure threshold decays at a slightly different rate from per-institution pressure variance, producing 50+ distinct values within one or two ticks regardless of whether the recovery branch (pressure < 0.3) is ever reached. A write-back where recovery is effectively dead code on this sample's pressure distribution would still pass slice 1's stated done-criteria while failing the 'tracks the pillar' claim ruling 2 makes about the mechanism.

severity_examples.condition: Becomes visible only across runs longer than the 193-day sampler window, so slice 1's own done-criteria would not surface it.
severity_examples.scenario: RECOVERY_PER_MONTH (0.005) is roughly a third of EROSION_LEG_PER_MONTH (0.015). On a substrate already showing 9x oil movement and 160 distinct stability-index values (real, ongoing volatility), this asymmetry means legitimacy trends toward the floor across long runs by construction, not because of any specific leadership event -- a tuning decision the seven rulings never name or justify as intended texture versus an unexamined v0-prior default.

success_hints: Works from the actual constants in pillar.rs (EROSION_EFF_PER_MONTH, EROSION_LEG_PER_MONTH, RECOVERY_PER_MONTH, the 0.6/0.3 thresholds, the 0.2/0.9 clamp) and the actual sample numbers (leadership_pressure 0.69, oil 42->389) rather than reasoning about the write-back in the abstract.

States explicitly, with a citation, whether leadership_pressure is closed-loop (fed by the same institutions' legitimacy) or open-loop (exogenous) -- the runaway argument stands or falls on this and should not be left ambiguous.

Distinguishes 'the stated criterion is met' from 'the mechanism works as ruling 2 intends' separately for each of the three slice-1 sampler numbers, rather than treating all three as equally strong evidence.

Proposes a concrete fix (a stronger done-criterion that requires the recovery branch to fire, a specific constant adjustment, a recommended additional sampler check) rather than only flagging instability as a risk.
Stays inside the numeric and dynamical behavior of ruling 2 and ruling 7 -- does not relitigate save-schema questions or slice ordering, which belong to other reviewers.
